five.t: **The fridge attacks reached Germany and Portugal.** Brussels calls it deliberate; US officials privately suspect Iran for the commissary freezers.
**Russia hit Ukraine's grid in 10 regions on US election day** with 289 drones, 59 cruise and 17 ballistic missiles. Abu Dhabi talks are set for 10–11 Nov.
**Tehran on the record:** Hormuz reopens on day two if Washington moves first. Vance says he and Trump “feel really good” about a settlement; Trump names Pickaxe Mountain.
**Posture options reach Hegseth on Friday;** NBC reports they include pulling at least 25,000 of about 80,000 US troops from Europe.
**The revised Dutch tax plan drops the defence levy and the fuel-duty rise for 2027** and delays box 3 to 2029. It still lacks a majority before the 12 Nov vote.

pick.t: If you read one thing: the cold-chain lead, now a force-protection question as well as a food one.

items.h: Qeshm strikes, a drone claim and talk of a settlement
items.body: A US official called Monday's strike on Qeshm Island “a defensive measure” against “Iranians using surface to air missiles against US assets”; The Wall Street Journal reported “limited strikes” on Iran in recent weeks. [9] Iran's state news agency IRNA reported that the Revolutionary Guards destroyed a US MQ-9 drone east of the strait. [10] Vice President JD Vance told CNN: “The president and I both feel really good” about a negotiated settlement. Trump told Fox News: “We might have to go after Pickaxe, but that's not a big deal,” and told Axios: “One way or the other, we will do something, but there is no rush.” [9, 10] Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says “on day two, the Hormuz Strait will reopen” if Washington meets Iran's conditions first; on Tuesday Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Iran “will not submit.” [11, 10]
items.next: Qatari mediators took a draft US–Iran text, under negotiation for eight days, to Tehran on Monday night; no deadline or next round is set. [9] A Chinese special envoy visits Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia in early to mid-November. [12]

items.h: Election-day barrage on the grid; Abu Dhabi talks on 10–11 Nov
items.body: Overnight Russia launched 289 drones and 59 cruise missiles; the Air Force says 257 drones, 49 cruise missiles and 3 ballistic missiles were downed. [13] President Zelensky put the ballistic total at 17: “It is very telling that all of this happened on the day of the U.S. congressional elections.” [14] The Energy Ministry counts energy sites hit in 10 regions, worst in Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr and Kharkiv, with emergency outages in Kyiv and six regions. [15] A strike on a Kharkiv hospital injured 73, and the toll from Monday's bombing of an aid point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, rose to 29, with 48 missing. [16, 17]
items.next: Envoy Steve Witkoff: “The United States will mediate working-level negotiations between Ukraine and Russia on 10-11 November in Abu Dhabi.” US negotiators meet France, Germany, Britain, the EU and NATO in Brussels this week. [18, 16]

items.h: Midterms: the first polls close at midnight CET
items.body: Republicans go in with narrow majorities in both chambers. [19] Polls close from 00:00 CET Wednesday in parts of Indiana and Kentucky, Pennsylvania at 02:00 CET and California at 05:00. [3] Tracking firms say Russia is posting AI-altered videos on X, among them a fabricated claim against Texas Senate nominee James Talarico; Iran has been “relatively quiet”. [20] Polling cited by CNBC puts support for the military action against Iran at 31%. [9]
items.next: Results overnight; Congress returns for the lame-duck session on 9 Nov, and the new Congress is seated on 3 Jan 2027. [19, 21]

items.h: Drones hit three more of Sudan's power stations
items.body: Drones on Monday hit the New Halfa and Aroma stations in Kassala state and Al-Ghazali near Merowe, a day after Abu Hamad and Al-Dabbah; Anadolu counts at least 16 stations hit in a week. [22] Sudan filed complaints against Ethiopia at the UN Security Council and the African Union, saying 187 drones in 70 attacks since February came from Ethiopian territory. [23]
items.next: The complaints sit with the UN Security Council and the AU Peace and Security Council; no session date is published. [23]

items.h: North Korea tests cluster warheads during allied drills
items.body: North Korea fired a tactical ballistic missile with a cluster-bomb warhead on 31 Oct and strategic cruise missiles with a cluster warhead on 2 Nov, according to the state agency KCNA, during allied drills. [24, 25] Taiwan's air force runs its Sky Dragon drills 2–6 Nov, and Kinmen held live-fire drills on Tuesday. [26, 27]
items.next: The Freedom Flag exercise at Kunsan runs to 6 Nov; Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders meet in Shenzhen on 18–19 Nov, and Taipei is still seeking a formal invitation. [24, 28]

feature.title: Tehran in its own words: two days, seven conditions
body: Five voices carry Iran's line. Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei has not appeared in public since the war began and speaks through written statements; Maj. Gen. Ahmad Vahidi commands the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). [29] Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf is chief negotiator, Abbas Araghchi is foreign minister, and Esmaeil Baghaei speaks for the ministry. [30, 31]

On 4 Oct Ghalibaf said the strait stays shut until seven conditions from the Islamabad memorandum are met. [30] In an Al Jazeera interview reported on 1 Nov, Araghchi listed them: US recognition of a new Iran–Oman shipping route, sanctions lifted, a smaller US military presence, oil waivers restored, frozen funds released including those in Qatar, all other routes closed, and an end to the war on every front, “especially Israel's attacks on Lebanon”. Under the two-day plan, Washington acts on day one and the strait reopens on day two. [11] Euronews's account of the plan on 2 Nov also lists an end to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports. [31]

On capabilities, the record is mostly claims. Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority requires ships to coordinate with it, and ships that refuse are attacked; the US Treasury says no new oil has loaded at Iranian terminals since 25 Aug. [32] The IRGC navy claims more than 20 operations against US warships, without evidence; the head of US Central Command said in late August that the recognised transit routes were “free of Iranian sea mines”. [33] Vahidi told the Supreme Leader weapons output is up “seven-fold”, a claim not independently verified. [29]
The table sets the dated statements side by side, oldest first.

leads.title: The fridge wave reaches Germany, and Washington points at Iran
leads.teaser: Stores in North Rhine-Westphalia and Portugal join the list, Brussels calls it deliberate, and US officials privately suspect Iran for the commissary freezers.
rows: Since the night of 1–2 Nov, stores in at least 11 countries have reported remote tampering with refrigeration, after France on 11–12 Oct; Belgium alone counts about 75 sites. [36, 42, 43]
Controllers are switched to defrost or set to about +50 °C, mostly at night or at weekends; Danfoss says the Dutch systems hit still used default passwords. [35, 36, 39]

A0 in Europe; Belgium's federal prosecutor has opened a criminal case. [42] Two people told Defense One that US officials suspect Iran-linked hackers of the commissary intrusions, a view that “could change”. [44]

EU Commissioner Christophe Hansen called it a “deliberate attempt to disrupt” the food supply; the Dutch National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) issued guidance. [45, 46] Rome's crisis meeting found “limited impact”. [47]
leads.sw: Baseline requirement 4 (food and water) now has a military mirror: ask the J4 which contracted cold storage in the Benelux and Germany is remote-managed, and who can take it offline at 02:00.

leads.title: Germany hardens its bases; rail plots surface
leads.teaser: Berlin cites suspected drone surveillance of US bases, and two rail cases point at the lines a reinforcement would use.
rows: Lt. Gen. Alexander Sollfrank, head of the Bundeswehr's Joint Operational Command, said on Sunday that Germany will tighten base security and expand counter-drone capability. [48]
The Nuremberg and Świdnica cases are in the incident log. [40, 41]
Day two of the national police readiness order (2–8 Nov); no incident reported. [49]
leads.sw: Plan reception, staging and onward movement (RSOM) timelines through Germany with slower gates and rail-security checks.

pattern: **Same door, more rooms:** 11 countries in two nights, all through internet-reachable controllers with default credentials or old software. [36, 39]
**Night and weekend timing:** hits land between 01:00 and 04:00 or over a weekend. [39, 50]
**Rail reconnaissance:** two cases in one week point at transport networks rather than shops. [40, 41]

europe.h: Election day: what allies fear, and Friday's options
europe.body: Five NATO diplomats told POLITICO that a Republican defeat could push President Trump toward more troops out of Europe, smaller payments into NATO's common funding and limits on the Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List (PURL), [51] At least four option sets on force levels go to Hegseth on Friday, with the full review in December; NBC reported that they include withdrawing at least 25,000 of about 80,000 US personnel in Europe. [52, 53] Congress requires a certification before the number drops below 76,000. [54]
europe.sw: A troop decision tied to a Ukraine deal reaches host nations as politics before it reaches them as a planning order.

europe.h: Poland's council meets on a US base, and argues about the court
europe.body: President Karol Nawrocki's National Security Council met behind closed doors at 15:00 with Prime Minister Donald Tusk present. Nawrocki opened by calling the government's moves on the Constitutional Tribunal a serious constitutional crisis; no decision on the base had been published by late afternoon. [4] Warsaw would pay $3–4 billion for a base of up to 5,000 more permanent troops, with Wrocław, Poznań, Bydgoszcz and Szczecin named as sites. [55] Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski called the meeting unnecessary and said Washington has asked Warsaw to wait for its decision, due by December. [56]
europe.sw: A paid-for permanent base is the posture review's easiest yes; expect western sites such as the Benelux garrisons to be asked to justify themselves.

euregio.h: A4 resurfacing between Langerwehe and Düren until spring
euregio.body: Work on the A4 toward Aachen started on Monday and runs until spring 2027; two lanes stay open each way, and the Rurscholle rest area closes from Wednesday. [57]
euregio.fy: Allow extra time on the Köln run, including for the Christmas markets.

euregio.body: Asphalt repairs on 4–5 Nov close parts of Koutenveld and Raadhuisstraat. [6]

dod.h: A $450 million loan for small drones; AUTOWARCOM still on paper
dod.body: On 2 Nov the Office of Strategic Capital signed a conditional loan commitment of up to $450 million with Neros, a US maker of small drones. [62] The Autonomous Warfare Command (AUTOWARCOM), announced on 30 Sep as a four-star combatant command, has a stand-up target of 1 Oct 2027, needs legislation and has no commander. [63, 64] The Army's three-star Futures and Autonomous Systems Command (FASCOM) stood up on 1 Oct and must field priority autonomous systems by FY2028. [65, 66]
dod.sw: Track which FASCOM systems reach V Corps first; JFC Brunssum's counter-drone planning inherits their numbers.

dod.h: Trump asks how Hegseth and Caine are doing
dod.body: The Atlantic reported on Sunday that Trump has asked allies how Hegseth and the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, Gen. Dan Caine, are performing after what some advisers call “rosy” Iran-war forecasts; the White House says he has “full confidence” in both. [67]
dod.sw: The same two men sign off the Europe posture options due on Friday.

news.h: Ukrainian drone scouts in Combined Resolve, which ends Wednesday
news.body: At the Joint Multinational Readiness Center in Hohenfels, 1st Armored Brigade, 1st Armored Division trains with more than 3,500 personnel from seven nations, among them about 50 Ukrainian soldiers who bring drone experience from the front. [68]
news.sw: Pull their brigade-level drone reconnaissance lessons into NATO Allied Land Command (LANDCOM) and JFC Brunssum work before FASCOM's own systems arrive.

congress.h: USAREUR-AF's next commander waits on the Senate floor
congress.body: Lt. Gen. Kevin D. Admiral, nominated to command US Army Europe and Africa (USAREUR-AF) and LANDCOM, has waited on the Senate floor since the Armed Services Committee reported him on 23 Sep (PN1188); Maj. Gen. Christopher Norrie has acted since 2 Jul. [69, 70, 71]
congress.sw: Nominations still pending at adjournment go back to the White House, which would leave USAREUR-AF under acting command into 2027.

congress.h: FY27 defence bill waits for the lame duck
congress.body: The House passed H.R. 8800 by 216–212 on 22 Jul; the Senate's S. 4784 failed cloture, 50–46, on 14 Jul, and there is no conference text. Congress returns on 9 Nov. [21, 72] The House bill renews the 76,000-troop floor in Europe. [73]
congress.sw: The 76,000 floor is the one legal brake on the posture review.

items.body: The FY27 active-component colonel board (MILPER 26-170) recesses about 5 Nov. [74]

items.h: 2027 pay raise: 5% or 3.6% at O-4 and above
items.body: The House NDAA gives 7% to E-5 and below, 6% to E-6 through O-3 and 5% to O-4 and above; the Senate a flat 3.6%, the statutory baseline. The winner applies from 1 Jan. [61, 75]

items.body: TRICARE Open Season runs 9 Nov to 8 Dec for family plan choice; doing nothing keeps the current plan. Dental and vision (FEDVIP) enrolment runs to 14 Dec. [76, 77]

items.h: Europe's Ukraine force rehearses in Poland from 9 Nov
items.body: Britain and France announced “Koalicja”, the first exercise of the Multinational Force–Ukraine: about 2,800 troops from 10 countries, 1,100 of them French and 300 British, Dutch, Belgian and German contingents among them, near Nowa Dęba in south-east Poland from 9 to 22 Nov. It is not a NATO operation and would deploy only after a ceasefire; French Gen. Armel Dirou and British Lt Gen. Tom Bateman co-lead it from Paris. [79, 80]
items.sw: It draws on the same Dutch, Belgian and German units JFC Brunssum plans with. Ask which of them are double-hatted to the NATO Force Model.

items.h: Bundestag committee weighs seven buys; Patriots reordered
items.body: The budget committee takes seven proposals above €25 million on 4 Nov, among them a revised Eurofighter contract (38 Tranche 4, 20 Tranche 5 from 2031, 15 refitted for electronic warfare), eight Role 2B field hospitals and SPIKE-ER2 missiles. [81] The procurement office has ordered two Patriot fire units to replace the two given to Ukraine in 2025; the ministry says missile stocks remain short. [82]
items.sw: Launchers return before interceptors do: air defence over German reception areas stays thin into 2027.

items.h: Lithuania fields its first GM200 counter-battery radar
items.body: Lithuania took delivery of its first Thales GM200 MM/C radar for its new national division; it locates artillery and tracks first-person-view (FPV) drones. [83, 84] NATO expects Lithuania to spend 5.33% of GDP on core defence in 2026, the highest in the alliance. [85]
items.sw: A Baltic division with its own counter-battery and counter-drone radar is a planning asset for the plans JFC Brunssum owns.

items.h: Belgium hands the first of seven minehunters to Bulgaria
items.body: Belgium transferred the minehunter BNS Bellis (M916) to Bulgaria at Zeebrugge on 3 Nov, renamed Briz; it is the first of seven ships under a Belgian–Dutch–Bulgarian agreement. [86]
items.sw: Benelux mine countermeasures thin out until the new Belgian–Dutch ships arrive.

items.h: A $1.08 billion next Patriot interceptor, and output to triple
items.body: The Army awarded Lockheed Martin $1.08 billion on 2 Nov to develop the PAC-3 Edge “Future Interceptor”, with a new seeker and a Northrop Grumman three-pulse motor; tests start in 2027 and fielding in 2031. [87] Lockheed delivered 620 PAC-3 MSE missiles in 2025 and plans about 2,000 a year by the end of 2030; a GEM-T line at Schrobenhausen in Bavaria opens at the end of 2026. [82]
items.sw: Interceptor supply, not launchers, sets how much of the rear area allied air defence can cover.

items.h: Russia scales up anti-jam antennas on its drones
items.body: Defense News reports that Russia's Kometa anti-jam satellite-navigation arrays are in mass use in 16-element form, 20-element arrays are entering serial production, and 32-element antennas have turned up on Shahed-type drones over Kyiv. Ukraine's military intelligence says Russian firms ordered more than 100,000 modules this year. [88]
items.sw: Counter-drone plans for NATO logistics nodes need spoofing and hard kill, not only jammers.

items.h: Rheinmetall adds passive drone detection to Skynex
items.body: Rheinmetall will build Silvus RFeye passive radio-frequency sensors into its Skynex gun system and Skymaster command network, so drones can be located without the system emitting. Skynex fires airburst rounds at 1,000 a minute out to 4 km. [89, 90]
items.sw: Passive detection lets a fixed headquarters defend itself without lighting up for Russian signals intelligence.

aperture.contrarian: Monday's oil drop prices a deal Washington has not accepted: Iran's plan needs the US to move first, and Trump is naming Pickaxe Mountain. [11, 9] The case for it holding: Qatari mediators carried a draft to Tehran on Monday night. [9]

A contracted cold store holding a corps rear area's blood products and chilled rations reports freezers at +12 °C and rising; its controllers are remote-managed through a cellular router. Stresses baseline requirements 4 and 5 (food and water, mass casualties). First call: the host-nation support cell.
aperture.question: Which host-nation support contracts in our area depend on remote-access controllers, and who in each nation can take them offline at night?

deep.title: “God forbid”: how Moscow tells the hybrid story
body: On Monday Sergei Shoigu, secretary of Russia's Security Council, said Putin has ruled out attacking Europe “three or four times in the past two months”, then added: “God forbid you live to see a day when Russia launches a hybrid war against you.” [91]

Heard from Moscow, the line does three jobs. It denies, keeping each incident below the level of a collective response. It threatens, implying that what Europe sees is not yet the real thing. And it recasts German base hardening as hysteria; a public told its alarm is overblown is slower to pay for resilience.

longread.title: The fiscal risks of bringing US troops out of Europe
longread.why: John Deni of the Army War College on what a drawdown below the 76,000 floor would cost, days before the options land. [54]

items.h: SemiAnalysis launches GDPx; the best model scores 12%
items.body: The research firm SemiAnalysis published GDPx on 2 Nov, a benchmark of long agentic tasks in 11 domains: chip design, cybersecurity, biology, finance, legal, quant trading, recursive self-improvement, hardware design, materials science, alignment and software engineering. Tasks run for up to eight hours and are scored pass@1 over three attempts, with every domain weighted equally; 14 specialist startups wrote the challenges. [92, 93] Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 leads at 12.0%, ahead of Google's Gemini 4 Carbon at 10.9% and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra at 9.6%. Gemini leads biology and software engineering, GPT-6 Astra self-improvement and materials science, and in finance and legal nearly every model scores zero under binary grading. SemiAnalysis says safety classifiers lowered some scores in cyber, biology and alignment, and plans updates every three to six months. [92, 93]

items.h: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5: 1.6 trillion parameters, 48 billion active
items.body: Meituan released LongCat-2.5 on 2 Nov, a multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 1.6 trillion total parameters, about 48 billion active per token, a one-million-token context window and outputs of up to 128,000 tokens, built for long agent runs over whole codebases. It is live in Meituan's chat service and API; open weights are promised but not yet out, and Meituan's claim to be “competitive with Claude Opus variants” comes without published scores or prices. [94, 95]

items.h: Tesla runs unsupervised robotaxi rides in Fort Worth
items.body: Tesla's Robotaxi service began fully unsupervised public rides in Fort Worth, Texas, at 06:00 local time on 2 Nov, with no safety monitor on board, using Model Y cars across about 143 square miles. Fort Worth is the seventh unsupervised city after Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando and Tampa; fleet size and fares were not published. [96]

items.h: Agility's Digit passes 100,000 totes at a GXO warehouse
items.body: Agility Robotics said on 2 Nov that its Digit humanoid has moved more than 100,000 totes at GXO's Georgia site since June 2024, a company figure; GXO signed for two more US sites, in Statesville, North Carolina and Lebanon, Tennessee, from early 2027. No unit counts were given. [97]

items.h: Revised tax plan: no defence levy in 2027, box 3 slips to 2029
items.body: The cabinet sent the amended 2027 tax plan to the Kamer today. It scraps the vrijheidsbijdrage, an extra tax on labour meant to raise €347 million for defence in 2027, to be replaced by cuts to tax benefits still to be agreed; moves the new box-3 tax on investment gains from 2028 to 2029, partly paid from a €3.1 billion reserve; and drops the rise in VAT on flowers and plants from 9% to 21% in 2028. [8]
items.fy: The line that reaches your wallet is fuel: the planned fuel-duty increase is out of the revised plan. [8]

items.h: Still no majority for Wednesday's debate
items.body: The debate is Wednesday and the vote Thursday 12 Nov. In the Tweede Kamer, ChristenUnie, 50Plus and Groep Markuszower could just about carry it; in the Eerste Kamer the cabinet still needs opposition votes from the left or the right. [8] Pro and Volt have walked away; JA21, SGP and BBB want commitments on asylum, nitrogen, abortion and surrogacy. [110]
items.fy: If the plan falls, the fuel-duty discount falls with it. [110]

items.h: Asylum: 74 municipalities now under state pressure, three in Limburg
items.body: Asylum minister Bart van den Brink put 11 more municipalities, including Gennep, Mook en Middelaar and Roerdalen, under active supervision of the asylum distribution law (Spreidingswet); The Hague can now house asylum seekers there and send the bill. [111]

items.h: Regional bus strikes possible from 17 Nov
items.body: FNV and CNV expect new strikes in regional bus transport from 17 Nov; members vote on the final offer in the week of 9 Nov. NS and Arriva train staff fall under other agreements. [112]
items.fy: Plan a backup for any school or work run that relies on a regional bus from 17 Nov.

items.h: Dutch Mountain Film Festival opens Friday
items.body: Mountain and adventure films in Heerlen and Aachen from 6 to 15 Nov; a photo exhibition opens on Thu 5 Nov at 16:00 at HuB.Kerkrade. About 10 minutes to the Heerlen screens. [114, 115]

items.h: A children's show at Kasteel Hoensbroek on Sunday
items.body: “Het Kasteel in rep en roer!” on Sun 8 Nov at 11:30 and 13:30, for ages 4 to 7. No advance booking: sign up at the desk on the day; included in admission. [116]

items.h: GLOW lights up Eindhoven from Saturday
items.body: The light-art festival runs 7–14 Nov on a walking route of about 5 km from Eindhoven Centraal, nightly 18:30–23:00, free. About 55 minutes away; go early on a school night. [117]

otd.title: On this day · 3 November 1944
otd.body: The 112th Infantry of the US 28th Infantry Division crossed the Kall gorge and took Schmidt, about 40 km from Heerlen, the deepest point of the first Hürtgen attack. A single logging trail and a bridge over the Kall served as both attack route and supply line, and nobody had sent a patrol down it first. German counterattacks drove the regiment back across the Kall by 8 Nov; the division lost 6,184 men in the battle. Source: David T. Zabecki, HistoryNet. [128]

culture.title: Sint-Hubertus, today
culture.body: Hubert, patron saint of hunters since the 11th century, has his feast on 3 November. Across Belgian and Dutch Limburg, priests bless bread rolls (“hubkes”), once eaten as protection against rabies, along with horses and dogs. In Wiemesmeer (Zutendaal), about 35 minutes away, the feast has been held on 3 November every year since 1947, with hunting horns and an animal blessing. [129]
